Control parameters of drmTMB

Source: R/drmTMBcontrol.R
drmTMBcontrol.Rd

Settings of the optimisation of drmTMB, passed as its argument control, e.g. drmTMB(..., control = drmTMBcontrol(restart = TRUE)) or control = list(restart = TRUE).

Usage

drmTMBcontrol(
  optimiser = c("nlminb", "optim"),
  method = c("L-BFGS-B", "BFGS", "CG", "Nelder-Mead"),
  iter.max = 1000,
  eval.max = 2000,
  optcontrol = list(),
  inner = list(),
  restart = FALSE,
  smallsample = TRUE
)

Arguments

optimiser

the optimiser: "nlminb" (default, nlminb) or "optim" (optim)

method

the method of optim: "L-BFGS-B" (default), "BFGS", "CG" or "Nelder-Mead"

iter.max

maximum number of iterations of the optimiser (iter.max of nlminb, maxit of optim)

eval.max

maximum number of evaluations of the objective function of nlminb

optcontrol

a list of further control parameters of the optimiser, the argument control of nlminb (e.g. rel.tol, x.tol, trace) or optim (e.g. reltol, factr, pgtol, trace, parscale); its iter.max, eval.max or maxit replace those above. The tolerances of optim are factr=1e5 (L-BFGS-B) and reltol=1e-10 (the other methods) unless given, close to rel.tol=1e-10 of nlminb.

inner

a list of control parameters of the inner optimisation of the random effects for the Laplace approximation, see the argument inner.control of MakeADFun, e.g. list(maxit=2000, tol10=1e-6)

restart

if TRUE, the fit is restarted once at the estimates and the better fit is kept, see Details

smallsample

if TRUE (default), gaussian and lognormal models without random effects, priors, bmdpar, correlation structure and variance function use the unbiased residual variance with n - p residual degrees of freedom and t quantiles, as lm, nls and drc; if FALSE, the maximum likelihood estimate and normal quantiles. See drmTMB.

Value

a list with control parameters

Details

The optimiser minimises the negative log-likelihood (with random effects, its Laplace approximation) over the fixed parameters, with the gradient from TMB, and for nlminb without random effects also the Hessian. The same settings are used for the refits of bootstrap, anova.drmTMB (test="boot"), bmdma and vcovrobust.

optim does not use the Hessian, and its methods other than "L-BFGS-B" do not allow bounds; models with bounds (the default lower bounds 0 of the multistage, nec, haldane, exponential and power models, see drmTMB, user bounds lower and upper, or priors with a bounded support) need method "L-BFGS-B"; the other methods give an error. Parameter values at which the negative log-likelihood is not finite (e.g. a negative b4 of the BMD parameterisation) are given a large finite value for optim.

With restart=TRUE, the model is fitted again starting at the estimates, which restarts the approximations of the optimiser (e.g. after a false convergence, a stop at a kink of the likelihood, or in a flat likelihood of a variance), and the better fit is kept: the restart if its negative log-likelihood is lower, or as low and it converged. This doubles the time of the fits at least, also of the bootstrap fits.

Examples

drmTMBcontrol(optimiser="optim", optcontrol=list(factr=1e5), restart=TRUE)
#> $optimiser
#> [1] "optim"
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "L-BFGS-B"
#> 
#> $iter.max
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $eval.max
#> [1] 2000
#> 
#> $optcontrol
#> $optcontrol$factr
#> [1] 1e+05
#> 
#> 
#> $inner
#> list()
#> 
#> $restart
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $smallsample
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
fit <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
              control = drmTMBcontrol(optimiser = "optim", restart = TRUE))
summary(fit)
#> Call:
#> drmTMB(form = rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic", 
#>     control = drmTMBcontrol(optimiser = "optim", restart = TRUE))
#> 
#> Model:  loglogistic, decreasing curve
#> Family: gaussian, identity link for the asymptotes
#> 
#> Number of observations: 24
#> Log-likelihood: -15.88 (df = 6), AIC: 43.76, BIC: 50.82
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>                Estimate Std. Error
#> b1:(Intercept)   0.3215      0.380
#> b2:(Intercept)   7.7605      0.193
#> b3:(Intercept)  -3.9301      2.194
#> b4:(Intercept)   2.2147      0.920
#> b5:(Intercept)  -0.7594      1.134
#> The asymmetry parameter b5 is on the log scale.
#> 
#> Residual standard deviation: 0.527 on 19 degrees of freedom
#> 
#> Optimiser: optim (L-BFGS-B): CONVERGENCE: REL_REDUCTION_OF_F <= FACTR*EPSMCH, maximum absolute gradient 1.8e-05
#> Restarted at the estimates: no better optimum
